text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government inquiry into the hijacking of an Air Malta flight on June 9 has concluded that parts of a fake bomb, including batteries, coiled wire and a switch were passed together in a bag through an airport X-ray machine without raising suspicion. The report called for increased vigilance by machine operators.
- Government announces police appointments with Commissioner George Grech retaining his post and deputy and assistant commissioners appointed to fill vacant positions.
- Malta Federation of Industry discusses new system replacing VAT. Estimates show costs for industry may rise between 3.5 and 7.5 percent.
- George Borg, chairman of the state-owned postal company Posta Ltd, has resigned, citing personal reasons. The company has been facing criticism over spending.
